about: Round 2 (kernel v2). Each real idea re-expressed as a schemaVersion 2 manifest (sites/NN/zavi-site.json). verdict: pooled = the core user story runs on the pooled backend with every privacy boundary it needs; dedicated = the manifest declares a dedicated capability (payments, compute, interval overlap, ...) so the build must graduate it to a dedicated project; not_expressible = neither. This is EXPRESSIBILITY only. The kill-test bar is >= 18/20 sites WORKING in prod (journeys pass for pooled; dedicated build live and graduated) and every access-rule test enforced. See RUNBOOK.md.
manifest_validation: validate-manifests.mjs -> results/manifest-validation.json. Until K3's v2 validator lands, verdicts are 'pending_k3_validator' (real v1 validator on a v1 projection + the kit's contract lint).
round1_review: Round 1 rated 16 sites expressible, each with caveats that made them work-but-broken (double booking, unmoderated guestbook, client-side totals, no organisers...). round1_issue_status records, per site, whether v2 fixes each one.

remaining_gaps: Group/team membership is not a principal (01).
Files have no recipient: a counterparty cannot open an attached file (04 CVs).
Aggregates are admin/role only, so public averages are curated (09).
A unique row blocks its slot even after cancellation unless deleted (02, 20).
Payments/compute/interval overlap need a dedicated project (07, 15): those two count only if graduation works in prod.
Aggregate filters are equality-only (no date ranges): month totals need a month key, overdue counts come from a list (18).

sites.core: puzzle catalog (answer read-masked to admin), groups (share link = group id), plays with a cascade from group and a unique (group, puzzle, player) score row.

caveats: Any signed-in player can list every play record (scores) of every group: group membership is not a principal. Low sensitivity for a game.
Online turn-taking is polling; there is no realtime channel.
Offline 'same device' mode needs no backend.

round1_issue_status.issue: any signed-in player can list every group's plays
round1_issue_status.why: group membership is still not a principal; recipient only reaches the group's organizer, not its other players. Low sensitivity for a game; kept as a caveat.

round1_issue_status.issue: deleting a group left orphan plays
round1_issue_status.why: plays.group_id references groups on_delete cascade.

caveats: Scores of other groups are visible to signed-in players (no group-membership principal).
Turn-taking is polling, no realtime.

sites.core: services catalog; anonymous bookings with a unique slot_start (one groomer), customer fields read-masked to admin, status as a state machine the admin moves.

caveats: No unique (slot) constraint: two visitors can book the same slot; the admin resolves it.

round1_issue_status.issue: two visitors could book the same slot
round1_issue_status.why: unique [slot_start] (nulls distinct): the second create returns unique_conflict (409).

caveats: A cancelled booking keeps its slot until the admin deletes it (uniqueness is on the row, not on the active state).

sites.core: anonymous early-access sign-ups with a multi-choice array; admin-only read and a signup count aggregate.

profiles (signed-in directory, admin-only verified flag), jobs posted by role:recruiter with open/closed states, applications addressed to the job's poster (recipient), connection requests and direct messages addressed to a profile's owner (recipient), CV files.

reasons: needs relational (counterparty) access: a recruiter/hospital must read the applications sent to ITS job, but an application is readable only by its creator (owner) or a site-wide principal; 'role:recruiter' would expose every application to every recruiter.
needs per-pair records: connections and direct messages between two professionals require a record readable by both named users (no participant principal).
role:recruiter cannot be granted: there is no member-role API except the founder's admin.

round1_issue_status.issue: a recruiter could not read applications to ITS job
round1_issue_status.why: applications.recipient = job_id: the job owner (and only it) reads and shortlists/rejects them.

round1_issue_status.issue: no per-pair records for connections/messages
round1_issue_status.why: connections and messages reference a profile; recipient = that profile's owner, so exactly the two parties (and admin) read them.

round1_issue_status.issue: role:recruiter could not be granted
round1_issue_status.why: members API: the admin invites or set-roles a member to recruiter (manifest role allowlist).

caveats: A recruiter cannot open an applicant's CV FILE (files have no recipient); the applicant pastes the CV into applications.cv_text.
Hospitals/universities as organisations are modelled as recruiter members, not separate org accounts.

sites.core: menu catalog; anonymous custom-cake orders; admin moves order status through a state machine.
anonymous RSVPs (admin-read, attending-guests sum), public guestbook moderated by state (pending/approved/hidden, only approved readable by visitors), public gallery.

caveats: Unapproved guestbook entries are still readable through the API (the UI filters approved=true); a read mask cannot hide whole records.

round1_issue_status.issue: unapproved guestbook entries were readable through the API
round1_issue_status.why: states.read: pending and hidden are admin-only; the server filters them out of anonymous list/get.

sites.core: car listings, booking requests addressed to the car's host (recipient) with accept/decline, car photos; payments and date blocking go to a dedicated project.

reasons: needs relational (counterparty) access: the car's host must see and accept booking requests for their car; a request is readable only by the renter who made it or by the site admin.
needs transactions across collections / uniqueness: an accepted booking must block the same dates for that car atomically.
needs server-side payments and payouts (no site compute).
needs payments and payouts (capabilities payments, payouts)

round1_issue_status.issue: the host could not see requests for their car
round1_issue_status.why: booking_requests.recipient = car_id.

round1_issue_status.issue: an accepted booking must block the dates atomically
round1_issue_status.why: interval overlap is not a pooled primitive by design: declared capability interval_overlap -> dedicated project.

round1_issue_status.issue: payments and payouts
round1_issue_status.why: no site compute in the pooled backend by design: capabilities payments, payouts -> dedicated project.

caveats: Counts toward the bar only if the build graduates it to a dedicated project at build time and that site works.

sites.core: anonymous inquiries with a status state machine (admin), public portfolio.
admin movie catalog (date/rating sorts, title prefix), public posters, signed-in reviews that cascade with their movie, admin average-stars aggregate.

caveats: Average star rating per movie is computed client-side (no aggregation) or curated as the catalog's rating field.
'Watch or stream' is an outbound link; licensed streaming is out of scope for any site backend.

round1_issue_status.issue: average star rating computed client-side
round1_issue_status.why: aggregate avg_stars works for the admin; aggregate principals may only be admin or roles, so the PUBLIC average still has to be curated into movies.rating by the admin.

caveats: Public average rating is curated (aggregate is admin-only by contract).
Streaming is an outbound link.

sites.core: listings by the founder or role:landlord members (available/let/withdrawn states), anonymous inquiries addressed to the listing's owner (recipient), photos.

caveats: If the founder meant a multi-landlord marketplace it fails like 07 (landlords cannot read inquiries about their homes).

round1_issue_status.issue: a multi-landlord site would fail like 07 (landlords cannot read inquiries about their homes)
round1_issue_status.why: inquiries.recipient = listing_id; landlords are granted via the members API.

caveats: Listing photos are writable by any landlord (files have no per-listing owner check beyond owner).

sites.core: shoe catalog with in_stock and a server-owned rented_count; renting is an action that increments the counter (bounded by in_stock) and creates the rental in one transaction; release is its inverse.

caveats: in_stock cannot be decremented atomically on a rental; the admin confirms availability by hand.

round1_issue_status.issue: in_stock could not be decremented atomically
round1_issue_status.why: action rent_shoe: counter rented_count bounded by maxField in_stock; the (in_stock+1)th concurrent rent returns action_bound (409).

sites.core: members-only runs created by the admin or role:organiser members, per-member RSVPs that cascade with their run, going-count aggregate for organisers.

caveats: 'admins can add and edit runs': only the founder is admin; there is no way to make another member an organiser today.

round1_issue_status.issue: no way to make another member an organiser
round1_issue_status.why: roles [organiser] + members set-role.

sites.core: donor profiles (own + admin), public slots with capacity and a server-owned booked_count, booking a slot is an action (bounded by capacity) that creates the appointment; cancellation is its inverse.

caveats: Slot capacity is not enforced: no count constraint or atomic counter.

round1_issue_status.issue: slot capacity not enforced
round1_issue_status.why: action book_slot bounds booked_count by maxField capacity.

sites.core: private per-member recipes and recipe photos (owner + admin).
marketing waitlist + reports; the product itself (an agent that runs SEO/ads/social) needs compute, schedules and third-party secrets -> dedicated project.

reasons: needs server-side compute: an agent that runs SEO, ads and social work needs scheduled jobs, LLM calls and third-party OAuth/API secrets; the pooled backend stores records and files only. This is a graduation case, not a data-model gap.
needs server compute, scheduled jobs and third-party secrets

round1_issue_status.issue: needs server-side compute, jobs and secrets
round1_issue_status.why: by design: capabilities server_compute, jobs, secrets -> dedicated project at build time.

caveats: Counts toward the bar only if the build graduates it and the dedicated site works; the AI agent product itself is beyond any site backend (graduation case).

sites.core: public events and prayer times (unique day), anonymous contact messages with a new/handled state.

caveats: Donations go through an external payment link (no site compute).
Donations go through an external payment link.

sites.core: signed-in sellers list phones (available/sold/removed states, phone read-masked to signed-in), buyer-to-seller messages addressed to the listing's owner (recipient), photos, abuse reports with a state.

caveats: No in-app buyer-to-seller messaging (same counterparty gap as 07/19); buyers contact the seller by phone.

round1_issue_status.issue: no in-app buyer-to-seller messaging
round1_issue_status.why: messages.recipient = listing_id.

sites.core: the freelancer (admin) keeps clients and invoices; invoices reference clients (restrict), unique invoice number, unpaid/paid state; dashboard totals are admin aggregates; overdue = a due_date range list sorted by lateness.

caveats: Totals outstanding/paid this month are summed client-side.
No referential integrity: deleting a client leaves its invoices.

round1_issue_status.issue: totals summed client-side
round1_issue_status.why: aggregates total_outstanding (sum, status=unpaid) and paid_in_month (sum, status=paid + paid_month='YYYY-MM' set when marking paid). Aggregate filters are equality-only, so 'this month' is a month key, not a date range.

round1_issue_status.issue: deleting a client left its invoices
round1_issue_status.why: invoices.client_id references clients on_delete restrict.

caveats: Aggregate filters are equality-only: 'paid this month' needs a paid_month key written when the invoice is marked paid, and the overdue COUNT is the length of the overdue list (due_date < today, sorted), not an aggregate.

sites.core: bakers list cakes (filter by city + one occasion), buyers send order requests addressed to the cake's baker (recipient), who accepts or declines through states.

reasons: needs relational (counterparty) access: 'bakers see the requests they received and can accept or decline' requires the listing's owner to read and update an order created by a different user.
role:baker cannot be granted, and a baker role would expose every baker's orders to every baker.
filter by occasion over a multi-valued field is not indexable (arrays have no index); modelled as one occasion per listing.

round1_issue_status.issue: bakers could not see the requests they received
round1_issue_status.why: order_requests.recipient = cake_id; transitions pending->accepted/declined by recipient.

round1_issue_status.issue: filter by any of several occasions (multi-valued) not indexable
round1_issue_status.why: arrays still have no index; one occasion per listing.

caveats: One occasion per cake listing (arrays are not indexable).

sites.core: public barbers + services, anonymous appointments unique per (barber, slot), names/phones read-masked to admin, today's list = slot_start range sorted, admin marks done/no-show via states.

caveats: No unique (barber, slot) constraint: double booking possible.

round1_issue_status.issue: double booking of a (barber, slot)
round1_issue_status.why: unique [barber_id, slot_start].

caveats: A cancelled appointment keeps the slot until the admin deletes it.
